MANDARIN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: MANDARIN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

2. In MANDARIN, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   B. Only memorise without using the language
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

3. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

4. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

5. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

6. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
7. In three clear sentences, explain Oral Expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

9. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

10. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

2. A — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral Expression; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

8. (4 marks)

9. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for Information; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

10. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for Fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
